title.narrative: Leveraging digital solutions for improved delivery of Maternal and Child Health Services

description.narrative: The Government of India launched the Anaemia Mukt Bharat (AMB) strategy in 2018, implementing a comprehensive 6×6×6 approach targeting six beneficiary groups through six interventions via robust institutional mechanisms. The strategy encompasses prophylactic iron-folic acid supplementation, periodic deworming, behaviour change communication, digital testing methods, food fortification, and treatment of non-nutritional causes. Despite extensive efforts, anaemia prevalence remains persistently high due to critical programme gaps including inadequate frontline worker training, poor inter-departmental coordination, supply chain irregularities, and limited epidemiological evaluation of different anaemia types. The segmented supply chain particularly affects last-mile delivery, with poor cooperation in reporting across schools and Anganwadi centres.UNDP, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, will pilot initiative to address these challenges through technological intervention. The project aims to strengthen AMB implementation by developing integrated IT platforms for haemoglobin tracking and supply chain management, leveraging the U-WIN digital architecture. UNDP, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, has launched the Bridging the Digital Health Divide initiative to address these challenges through technological intervention.
